Subject: Questions on pricing waterfall & cross-border tax responsibility

Hi Mateo —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and legal asked me to confirm a couple of things before we sign:

1) Pricing waterfall: your order form shows a staircase of minimum commits by quarter. We need clarity on how unused credits are handled if we miss the ramp (refund vs. credit).
2) Tax / invoicing: our legal team wants to know which entity Redwood will invoice for US vs EU usage and who is responsible for VAT/withholding.
3) Net terms: the order form currently shows Net30 but Finance prefers Net45 for enterprise deals.

Can you send a redline path and a proposed invoicing flow that separates EU entity invoices? Procurement would like a clean runbook so we can attach a PO.

Also attaching our standard PO template for reference (attachment: LH_PO_template.pdf).

Thanks — can you get back by EOD Friday?

Sally
Sally Choi
Dir. Procurement, LedgerHealth

Hi Sally —

Appreciate the precise list — that helps. Quick summary of next steps from our side:

- I'll own the commercial write-up and a revised order form that explicitly calls out credit treatment for ramp shortfalls (option A: credit carry-forward for 12 months; option B: pro-rata refund on request).
- Kim (legal) will produce a short MSA redline that clarifies invoicing entities + tax/residency language and suggests a gross-up clause or reverse-charge allocation.
- Ben (Sales) will propose a pragmatic compromise on net terms (Net45 for annual contract value above threshold, otherwise Net30).
- We'll split invoicing by billing entity and provide an appendix that maps product usage to invoice entity by region.

I attached a working pricing schedule (pricing_schedule_RLW-0421.xlsx) and will circulate a redlined MSA draft by tomorrow morning. If LedgerHealth can confirm whether USD invoices are acceptable for the EU entity (LedgerHealth Europe will accept USD to avoid FX issues), that will speed things up.

On timing: aiming to get a consolidated Order Form + MSA redlines to you by EOD tomorrow so procurement/legal can do a single pass. If that works, please confirm PO timeline.

Thanks —
Mateo

Subject: RE: Questions on pricing waterfall & cross-border tax responsibility

Sally / team —

Attaching a redlined MSA (Redwood_MSA_v2_redlined.docx). High-level notes from Legal:

- Invoicing entity: Redwood proposes to invoice LedgerHealth US for all US-region usage; invoice LedgerHealth Europe (legal entity: LedgerHealth B.V.) for EU-region usage. We'll include an Appendix A mapping services by region to entity.
- VAT / withholding: we propose the default is that LedgerHealth is responsible for local indirect taxes (VAT/GST) and Redwood will issue gross invoices; if local law requires withholding, LedgerHealth will provide documentation (tax residency certificate) and Redwood will gross-up or issue a credit per Section 5.3 in the redline.
- Net terms: Legal is neutral on Net30 vs Net45; commercial can set Net45 as an exception on the order form when ACV >= $250k. I added a handoff clause requiring a PO number on first invoice.
- Pricing waterfall: added a clear definition for "Unused Credits" — default is carry-forward for up to 12 months; customer may request a refund for unused credits up to 30 days after contract end (refund subject to tax withholding).

Open items that need commercial direction: currency for EU invoices (USD vs EUR), and whether LedgerHealth requires separate invoice recipients for R&D vs production units.

I'll highlight the clauses on pages 7-9 of the redline. If we get confirmation on currency and PO timing, we can lock the language and provide a final PDF for signature.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Sally —

Thanks for the clear ask. Commercial proposal to enable sign today while minimizing legal churn:

- Pricing waterfall: we will publish a "Staircase Credit" table on the order form with three ramp phases (Q1 60%, Q2 80%, Q3 100%). Unused credits automatically carry forward for 12 months. Refunds will be available on an exception basis (credit applied by default).
- Net terms: Redwood will accept Net45 for this deal (deal_id RLW-2024-0421) provided LedgerHealth issues a PO referencing the Net45 clause and ACV >= $275k. Otherwise default Net30 applies.
- Invoicing split: Redwood will issue monthly invoices in arrears to the mapped entity. For EU usage, invoices will be sent to LedgerHealth B.V., in USD unless LedgerHealth requests EUR. If LedgerHealth requires withholding gross-up, we'll handle via the tax-responsibility appendix.
- Activation credits / prepay: propose a $75k prepay credit reserve that can be drawn down; any remaining prepay after 12 months is refundable or can be converted to credits.

Please confirm: (A) EU entity is LedgerHealth B.V. and (B) whether they want invoices in EUR. If yes to EUR, we'll convert the pricing schedule and issue EUR invoices with FX clause.

If we get PO and confirmation on currency today, we can generate the final order form and push to DocuSign by tomorrow.

Ben Carter
Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

- Currency: LedgerHealth Europe prefers EUR invoices for tax reconciliation. US invoices should remain USD.
- Withholding / tax certificates: we'll provide tax residency certificates for LedgerHealth B.V. and expect Redwood to apply reverse-charge where applicable; if local law requires withholding, procurement will supply forms and we accept the gross-up handling outlined in your redline.
- PO timing: procurement will provide a PO by COB Monday (PO will reference RLW-2024-0421 and Net45 exception).

Requested deliverables: final Order Form (with staircase table, carry-forward default, refund exception) and an Appendix A mapping usage to invoice entity (US vs EU), plus the redlined MSA incorporated. Please provide the final packet and DocuSign link by EOD Monday.
